# `never-loop`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: correctness · Profile: none · Default: warning · Fixes: none · Options: none

Reports a `while` or `for` loop whose body ends with an unconditional `break` or
`return` and has no `continue` for the loop, so it never runs a second
iteration.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

A loop whose body always leaves on its first pass runs at most once, so it is
an `if` in disguise. More often than not that is a mistake: a `return` or
`break` meant for the code after the loop was placed inside it, or an exit
meant to be conditional lost its `if`. A search such as
`for (items) |item| { if (item.id == id) return item; return null; }` looks
at only the first element.

## When it fires

It reports a `while` or `for` loop whose body (the block's last statement, or
the single statement of a braceless body) is an unconditional `return`, a
`break` without a value, or a `continue` that targets an outer loop, when
nothing in the body continues this loop: no unlabeled `continue` outside a
nested loop and no `continue` naming this loop's label.

Shapes that use a loop deliberately stay quiet: `inline` loops; loops with an
`else` branch, which read as the `if`/`else` they are; a `break` that carries
a value (`for (items) |item| break item;`); a `break` that only leaves a
labeled block forming the body; and the breakable-block idiom
`while (true) { ...; break; }`, although a labeled block says the same thing
more plainly.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
fn firstEven(values: []const u32) ?u32 {
    for (values) |value| {
        if (value % 2 == 1) return null;
        return value;
    }
    return null;
}
```
